report.summary: Chunk 2 of 3: defines abstract_fingerprint, token_bag, CloneMemo, unit_clusters, window_runs, window_clusters_from_runs, window_clusters, renamed_clusters, _overlap, _candidate_pairs, and constants. Code is present and consistent.
risks: TYPE3_EXCLUDED_LANGUAGES | medium | C/C++ excluded from Type-3 pass due to limited keyword set causing false positives; cluster fabrication risk if admitted without extending _GENERIC_KEYWORDS. | Verify that _GENERIC_KEYWORDS (not in this chunk) is extended before removing exclusion.

_candidate_pairs pair_cap | medium | pair_cap may truncate candidate pairs early, potentially missing some true positives in large corpora. | Review whether pair_cap is set to a value that balances performance and recall.

window_runs order dependency | low | The order of returned hashes is load-bearing for deterministic output; if the input order changes, cluster output may change. | Ensure runs_by_file list order matches original file order.

CloneMemo caching by id(u) | low | Using id() for caching assumes CodeUnit objects are not reused across calls; if same object is reused, id may collide, but scope is one build_index call so low risk. | Confirm that memo is scoped per build_index call.

renamed_clusters recomputes exact_fp | medium | Comment says recomputation is wasted, but memo caches it, so actually not wasted if memo is shared. | Verify memo is passed correctly to avoid recomputation.
window_clusters_from_runs run_owners uses set | low | Using set for run_owners values loses ordering information, but order is not needed for cross-file grouping. | No action needed.

handoff.purpose: Defines fingerprint functions, CloneMemo caching class, and cluster computation functions for exact, renamed, and near-miss clone detection.

symbols.name: abstract_fingerprint
symbols.note: Returns 12-char SHA1 of abstracted tokens from source.

symbols.name: token_bag
symbols.note: Returns Counter of abstracted tokens for near-miss overlap.

symbols.name: CloneMemo
symbols.note: Caches exact and abstract fingerprints per unit to avoid recomputation.

symbols.name: CloneMemo.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes empty caches and stores spec_by_lang.

symbols.name: CloneMemo._spec
symbols.note: Returns LanguageSpec for a CodeUnit's language.

symbols.name: CloneMemo.exact_fp
symbols.note: Returns cached or computed exact fingerprint for a unit.

symbols.name: CloneMemo.abstract_fp
symbols.note: Returns cached or computed abstract fingerprint for a unit.

symbols.name: CloneMemo.put_abstract_fp
symbols.note: Stores a precomputed abstract fingerprint for a unit.

symbols.name: unit_clusters
symbols.note: Clusters units by exact fingerprint, returns sorted list of cluster dicts.

symbols.name: window_runs
symbols.note: Returns distinct normalized run hashes for one file.

symbols.name: window_clusters_from_runs
symbols.note: Cross-file clustering from precomputed per-file run hashes.

symbols.name: renamed_clusters
symbols.note: Clusters units by abstract fingerprint, excluding pure Type-1 groups.

symbols.name: _overlap
symbols.note: Computes multiset overlap ratio for near-miss similarity.

symbols.name: _candidate_pairs
symbols.note: Generates candidate unit pairs for near-miss comparison using inverted index.

symbols.name: _MIN_BAG
symbols.note: Minimum abstract token count to consider a unit for near-miss.

symbols.name: _ANON
symbols.note: String constant for anonymous units to exclude from near-miss.

symbols.name: TYPE3_EXCLUDED_LANGUAGES
symbols.note: Set of languages excluded from Type-3 near-miss pass.

claims.text: Multiset of ABSTRACTED tokens — the SourcererCC bag used for near-miss (Type-3) overlap.
claims.why: token_bag returns Counter of abstract tokens; near_clusters function uses such bags for overlap.

claims.text: Abstracted (not raw) so a near-copy with renamed locals still overlaps heavily.
claims.why: Abstract tokens ignore identifier names, so renamed locals still match.

claims.text: Per-unit derived fingerprints, computed once and shared by all three clone passes.
claims.why: CloneMemo caches fingerprints and is passed to unit_clusters, renamed_clusters, and near_clusters.

claims.text: ``unit_clusters`` computes the exact fingerprint; ``renamed_clusters`` computed that exact fingerprint AGAIN (it needs it to exclude pure Type-1 clusters) plus the abstract one; ``near_clusters`` then derived the abstract one a third time.
claims.why: unit_clusters calls memo.exact_fp; renamed_clusters calls memo.exact_fp and memo.abstract_fp; near_clusters (not in chunk) would use abstract fingerprint.

claims.text: ONLY the two 12-char fingerprints are cached, never the token lists.
claims.why: Cache stores tuple (unit, fp_str); token lists are not stored.

claims.text: The lists are the memory-heavy part -- ``all_units`` already retains full source text at ~22.5x source bytes -- and they are needed only *within* ``near_clusters``, which derives its bag and its fingerprint from a single tokenization.
claims.why: Reference to all_units and source text size ratio is outside chunk.

claims.text: Each entry holds a reference to its unit alongside the value, so an ``id()`` key can never be recycled onto a different object while the memo is alive.
claims.why: Cache stores tuple (unit, fp); id(u) is key; unit reference prevents id reuse across objects.

claims.text: Scope one memo to one ``build_index`` call and drop it after: a module-level cache would leak across scans.
claims.why: Reference to build_index is outside chunk.

claims.text: Donate a fingerprint derived from tokens the caller already had.
claims.why: Method stores provided fp if not already cached.

claims.text: ``near_clusters`` must tokenize anyway to build its bag, so it gets the abstract fingerprint for free and hands it back rather than leaving a later pass to re-abstract the same source.
claims.why: near_clusters is not in this chunk.

claims.text: memo=None keeps every standalone caller (tests, the CLI, a single pass called on its own) working exactly as before -- it just gets a private memo instead of a shared one.
claims.why: Code creates new CloneMemo if memo is None.

claims.text: Split out of ``window_clusters`` so it can run in a worker process: this is the per-file, embarrassingly-parallel half.
claims.why: window_runs is a pure function taking text and spec, suitable for parallel execution.

claims.text: The ORDER of the returned list is load-bearing — the caller replays it into ``run_owners``, whose insertion order decides the tie-break order of the final (stable-sorted) cluster list. Returning a set here would make the output nondeterministic.
claims.why: Function returns list in first-encounter order; set would lose order.

claims.text: Cross-file half of the window pass, over precomputed per-file run hashes.
claims.why: Function takes runs_by_file and produces clusters.

claims.text: ``runs_by_file`` must be in the original file order and each run list in first-encounter order (see ``window_runs``) — that reproduces exactly the insertion sequence the single-pass implementation produced.
claims.why: Function uses insertion order of run_owners (defaultdict of set) which preserves order of keys from first insertion.

claims.text: Now a composition of the per-file (``window_runs``) and cross-file (``window_clusters_from_runs``) halves; behaviour is unchanged.
claims.why: window_clusters calls window_runs then window_clusters_from_runs.

claims.text: Clusters of units that share an ABSTRACT fingerprint (identical up to renamed identifiers/literals) but are NOT already byte-identical exact clones.
claims.why: Function groups by abstract fingerprint and filters out groups with only one distinct exact fingerprint.

claims.text: We exclude clusters explained entirely by exact cloning (all members share one exact fingerprint) so this reports *renamed-but-not-identical* only — the genuine Type-2 signal, additive to ``unit_clusters``.
claims.why: Skip groups where len({exact_of[id(u)] for u in group}) < 2, i.e., all same exact fp.

claims.text: Multiset overlap = |A intersect B| / |smaller bag|. 1.0 means the smaller bag is fully contained in the larger; the SourcererCC similarity measure.
claims.why: Code computes inter = sum((a & b).values()), denom = min(sum(a.values()), sum(b.values())), returns inter/denom.

claims.text: C/C++ were excluded by ACCIDENT until _ts_name learned to read `declarator`: every C unit was named "<anonymous>" and the _ANON filter below dropped it. Naming them removes the accident, so the exclusion has to become deliberate or it silently becomes an admission.
claims.why: Reference to _ts_name and _ANON filter behavior is outside chunk.

claims.text: It is not safe yet: _GENERIC_KEYWORDS has no C type system (int/char/unsigned/sizeof/typedef/struct/volatile/template/...), so C's abstracted alphabet collapses to ~16-22 symbols and unrelated functions score 0.72-0.90 pairwise -- above the 0.8 threshold.
claims.why: _GENERIC_KEYWORDS and threshold not in chunk.

claims.text: Admitting C requires extending _GENERIC_KEYWORDS plus a green false-positive suite; until then, fabricating clusters is the worse error, so C/C++ stay out and index.py REPORTS the exclusion rather than returning a silent zero.
claims.why: Reference to index.py and false-positive suite outside chunk.

claims.text: Small corpora: all pairs. Large corpora: a SourcererCC-style inverted index token->units, so only units sharing a rare token are ever compared — the O(n^2) blow-up is never paid.
claims.why: If n <= 60, returns all pairs; else builds inverted index and only pairs units sharing a rare token.

claims.text: ``rare[i]`` is unit i's rare-token SET.
claims.why: Parameter named rare, type list[set].

observations.what: window_runs uses spec.line_comment to identify comment lines; if spec is None, defaults to ("//", "#").
window_runs skips lines that start with a comment marker, but only checks startswith; inline comments after code are not removed.
window_runs requires len(line) > min_line_len (default 3) to include the line.
window_clusters_from_runs uses defaultdict(set) for run_owners; insertion order is preserved for keys (Python 3.7+), but values are sets, so order within a set is not preserved.
renamed_clusters recomputes exact_of for each unit even if memo is used; memo caches exact_fp, so it's not recomputed but still calls memo.exact_fp for each unit.
_candidate_pairs has a pair_cap parameter that can limit the number of pairs; if pair_cap is reached, early return may miss some pairs.
TYPE3_EXCLUDED_LANGUAGES is a set of strings; exclusion is checked in near_clusters (not in this chunk).
